cards.title: Set a defensible email revenue benchmark and KPI case
cards.summary: Use the source's 30%-of-total-store-revenue benchmark to justify email investment and frame email as CAC and LTV leverage rather than a channel experiment.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much resource to put into email lifecycle, or building the internal case for hiring/agency/tooling spend.
steps: Frame the target at store level, not marketing level: the source states email should drive at least 30% of total ecommerce revenue (not 30% of marketing-attributed revenue). Treat this as the source's heuristic target, not a universal law — some catalogues and repeat-purchase categories will sit far above or below it.

Argue the three strategic benefits the source gives: (1) it lowers blended customer acquisition cost because paid traffic lands on site and converts to subscribers you can convert later for free; (2) it raises LTV through engineered repeat purchases instead of hoping customers return; (3) it builds an owned audience that compounds and reduces dependence on Meta/Google/TikTok CPMs and algorithm changes.

Map the counterfactual risk to your store: if the ad platform's CPMs double or your account is restricted tomorrow, how much of your revenue base can you still contact directly? That gap is your email opportunity size.

Translate the target into a monthly revenue number and compare against your current email-attributed revenue using a defined attribution window so the gap is measured consistently (see attribution card).
caveats: 30% is the presenter's stated benchmark from agency work, not a published industry statistic.
Changes to attribution windows will change the measured percentage; be consistent or compare like-for-like.

cards.title: Complete the Klaviyo–Shopify integration and sync settings
cards.summary: Wire Shopify into Klaviyo correctly so subscriber capture, event tracking and anonymous activity all flow into one profile record.
cards.use_when: Initial account setup, a re-platform migration, or auditing why checkout/pop-up subscribers and browse events are missing from Klaviyo.
steps: During signup select 'sell products online', choose Shopify as the primary platform, and enter your Shopify URL. If migrating from another platform (e.g. Mailchimp), declare your existing list size so Klaviyo can guide sending-limit warmup; if new, select that you have no contacts.
Set your sender name (brand name, or 'Founder at Brand') and sender email address. This is what appears in the inbox, so it drives open behaviour as much as the subject line.
Turn on the Shopify app embed for on-site tracking inside your Shopify theme; without it Klaviyo cannot see on-site events.
Check 'sync your Shopify email subscribers to Klaviyo' and point them into your single main email list; mirror the same for SMS subscribers into one main SMS list.
Leave 'sync profiles and custom properties from Klaviyo to Shopify' unchecked — the source sees no strong reason for most brands to push Klaviyo data back into Shopify.

In Klaviyo data settings, enable anonymous visitor tracking. By default, views and add-to-carts before an email is captured are invisible, which suppresses browse-abandonment and cart-abandonment volume. Verify the current toggle location in your account, as the UI changes.
caveats: Anonymous visitor tracking means pre-opt-in behaviour becomes attached to the profile once they identify — disclose this in your privacy policy where required.
Menu names and toggles in Klaviyo change; confirm the current interface before instructing a team member.

cards.title: Configure smart sending and attribution windows
cards.summary: Set the smart-sending window and choose attribution windows that match your consideration cycle, then exclude inflated data sources from reporting.
cards.use_when: Initial account configuration, or when email revenue reporting looks implausibly high/low and you need defensible numbers.
steps: In Settings > Email > Sender preferences, keep Smart Sending ON with the default 16-hour window so a subscriber does not receive a campaign within 16 hours of another email. This is the source's recommended default; it is customisable per brand.
Decide on 'ignore transactional messages': the source typically leaves this unchecked for most brands, meaning a just-purchased customer can still receive a marketing campaign.

Set open/click attribution windows to reflect your consideration cycle. Klaviyo's default is 5-day open / 5-day click. The source advises shorter for impulse-purchase products and longer for long-consideration products (e.g. $10k furniture with a ~30-day decision), but says do not stray far outside the 5/5 default as a conservative anchor.
In tracking/reporting exclusions, exclude transactional messages from attribution so order confirmations do not show up as revenue-driving email.

Exclude bot clicks (email and SMS) and exclude Apple Mail Privacy Protection opens from attribution data — since iOS 15, Apple pre-opens mail, generating fake opens that would otherwise claim credit for purchases.
Save, then re-check the reporting figures so you know whether your previous baseline was inflated.
caveats: Attribution windows determine how much credit email claims; changing them changes the 30% revenue KPI and all subsequent comparisons.
Apple privacy opens still appear in open-rate metrics generally unless filtered — for engagement segments, always filter with 'Apple privacy open is false'.

cards.title: Set brand defaults, fonts and fallbacks for email design
cards.summary: Load logo, colours, socials and custom fonts with websafe fallbacks so every email and consent page renders on-brand across inboxes.
cards.use_when: Setting up Klaviyo for the first time, or when emails render in the wrong typeface or look unbranded on some devices.
steps: In the brand library, upload your logo — it appears in email headers and sometimes footers.
Set brand colours for accent, body text, buttons and links so templates inherit a consistent palette.
Set your primary font. Klaviyo does not support custom fonts natively for all inboxes; it supports websafe fonts, so pick the closest websafe match as the account default.
Add custom fonts separately. Google fonts and Adobe fonts can be selected directly. Fully custom fonts require the 'hosted web font' route with Klaviyo's hosting instructions.
Always define a fallback font — inbox providers such as Gmail may only render Google/web fonts, so an Adobe or bespoke typeface will silently substitute. Choose the closest visual match.
Add social icons in the brand settings so footers populate automatically without manual entry in every template.
Set brand voice if you use Klaviyo's AI copywriting, so generated copy matches tone.
caveats: Header links are rarely useful for most brands given the design approach shown in the course; they can be skipped.
Font rendering varies by inbox client; the fallback is what most recipients will actually see.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Authenticate your domain: dedicated sending domain, SPF, DKIM, DMARC
cards.summary: Stand up a branded sending subdomain with DNS records to protect sender reputation, and keep DMARC policy at p=none to avoid self-inflicted spam filtering.
cards.use_when: New Klaviyo account, domain migration, or diagnosing poor inbox placement despite good content.
steps: In Settings > Domains > Add domain, enter your root domain (e.g. brand.com) and then create a sending subdomain such as send.brand.com. This isolates marketing sending reputation from your root domain.
Choose the setup path: Klaviyo may offer an assisted integration partner (the source notes an 'Entry' integration option and that it may cost money); otherwise set up manually.

Select your domain provider, copy the generated DNS records (name and value) into your host's DNS settings (e.g. GoDaddy), then click verify. Verification can take up to 48 hours — only verify after records are actually published.
Add the SPF, DKIM and DMARC records the same way. SPF, DKIM and DMARC tell inbox providers you are who you claim to be and protect your brand from spoofers.

Critical: when creating the DMARC record, ensure the policy reads p=none, not reject or quarantine. With reject/quarantine, any email the provider thinks is spam goes straight to spam; with none, it continues to be delivered to inboxes. The source calls this a huge difference in delivered mail.
Confirm SPF/DKIM/DMARC are all passing before scaling volume.
caveats: The source presents p=none as the safer setting for deliverability; security teams may prefer stricter policies, which can suppress delivery.
DNS record formats and provider UIs differ; verify current instructions before editing live DNS.
DNS propagation delays mean urgent sends may go out unauthenticated if you leave setup to the last minute.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Maintain sender reputation with bounce, spam and engagement thresholds
cards.summary: Treat sender reputation like a credit score and monitor the three inputs — bounce rate, spam complaints and engagement — against the source's thresholds.
cards.use_when: Ongoing deliverability monitoring, or when opens collapse and you need to diagnose reputation damage.
steps: Understand the model: reputation is history-based and hard to rebuild once damaged; a good reputation gets primary inbox placement, a bad one gets spam or promotions tab.

Keep bounce rate under 1%. Bounces come from invalid addresses — e.g. a fake email submitted through a pop-up form still triggering the welcome or abandoned-cart flow. Suppress hard-bouncing addresses and consider preventing obviously fake form entries.

Keep spam complaint rate below 0.3%, and ideally below 0.1%, to stay inside Gmail and Yahoo's stricter 2024+ requirements. Locate these rates in your account reporting and review on a regular cadence.
Maximise positive engagement signals: opens, clicks and especially replies tell inbox providers people want to hear from you. Low opens and low clicks act as negative signals.
Send at a consistent cadence — the source cites an example of two campaigns a week plus flows sending daily — because erratic sending (long silence then a burst) is treated as a negative signal.
Fix the root cause before re-sending: low opens usually means wrong audience (see 180-day cleaning and engagement segments), not a subject-line problem.
caveats: Thresholds (0.3% complaint, 0.1% ideal, 1% bounce) are the source's targets and align with stated Gmail/Yahoo expectations; Google's published requirements should be checked for current limits.
Reputation damage is slow to reverse, so prevention, not remediation, is the practical strategy.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Clean unengaged subscribers and use engagement-tiered segments
cards.summary: Suppress subscribers inactive for 180+ days and work in 14/30/60/90-day engagement windows to protect primary inbox placement.
cards.use_when: Replenishment/list hygiene work, or when deliverability declines from sending to a stale list.
steps: Define the benchmark: suppress profiles inactive past 180 days. Someone who signed up two years ago and has not opened, clicked or visited since is near-certainly uninterested, and every send to them dilutes your reputation.

Build engagement filters using Klaviyo's activity windows rather than one blunt list. The source's framework uses 14-day, 30-day, 60-day and 90-day active windows to grade engagement tiers, letting you send the most aggressive cadence to the freshest tiers and reduce or suppress the tail.
Within the engaged segment, always filter out fake signals: require 'opened email where Apple privacy open is false' OR 'clicked email where bot click is false'.

Add recency carve-outs before suppressing: someone who subscribed in the last 14 days, or was active on site in the last 14 days, should stay in the engaged segment even with no opens — they may only have received one or two emails, or may be re-showing intent.
Put a time limit on the carve-out: if a site-active subscriber does not engage within roughly two weeks, they should drop back out rather than staying engaged status for six months on one visit.
Re-run the suppression periodically rather than once, so the tail is pruned continuously.
caveats: Suppression reduces list size and short-term sends; the source frames this as necessary for future inbox placement rather than a loss.
Engagement tiers only work if open/click tracking is filtered for Apple and bot events, otherwise inactive people will look engaged.

cards.title: Customise consent, preference and unsubscribe pages, and use single opt-in
cards.summary: Brand the four consent pages and choose single opt-in over double opt-in to avoid losing a large share of subscribers at the confirmation step.
cards.use_when: Account setup, when signup-to-list conversion is poor, or when unsubscribes look unbranded and abrupt.
steps: In Settings > Other, locate the four pages: preference page, subscribe page, email confirmation, and unsubscribe page.

Edit the preference page with Klaviyo's drag-and-drop editor (text, images, background colour, button colour) so a subscriber who wants fewer emails can pick topics instead of leaving entirely. You are legally required to let people update preferences or unsubscribe.
Edit the unsubscribe page to add brand-appropriate copy (e.g. a thank-you for being part of the brand) rather than a bare default page.

Set single opt-in rather than double opt-in. The source is emphatic here: with double opt-in, subscribers must click a confirmation email before receiving anything, and most people never click it, so you lose a large share of signups. The subscribe and email confirmation pages then become unnecessary to edit.
Check the footer of your email templates includes working preference and unsubscribe links.

If a person reports still receiving emails after unsubscribing, use the profile's three-dot menu > Suppress to remove them from all sends — a genuinely unsubscribed person receiving mail is a spam-complaint risk.
caveats: Single opt-in is the source's recommendation on volume grounds; double opt-in is stronger for consent quality and some regions' compliance expectations. GDPR-style consent rules may override the list-growth argument.
Suppression and unsubscribe are different states; both must be respected.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Map the customer journey before building flows and campaigns
cards.summary: Sequence every touchpoint — ad/organic, pop-up, welcome, campaigns, first purchase, repeat — so messages match what the subscriber already knows.
cards.use_when: Planning lifecycle architecture, or when you suspect campaigns and flows are contradicting each other.
steps: Trace the source's journey structure: first visit from Meta/organic/TikTok → pop-up form offer → first emails from automated flows (welcome/nurture, or abandoned cart if applicable) → recurring campaigns at least weekly → first order → post-purchase messaging designed to drive the next order.

At the pop-up checkpoint, check the ad or content creative the visitor arrived from, then write the pop-up offer to speak only to what that traffic already knows. Mismatched offers are the most common journey break.

Audit for cross-channel contradiction: the source's example failure is a first-time-customer discount sent to someone who has already placed five orders, which annoys and is unusable. Gate first-purchase offers to non-purchasers.
Assign each touchpoint a single job and audience stage so content, offer and copy align with where the person is.
Review flows and campaigns together on a schedule — this is the fix for the common pattern of channels being built 'in a silo'.
caveats: The journey is described as a typical sequence; not every store has a pop-up-first entry or a long nurture phase.
Journey logic is qualitative — treat it as an alignment discipline rather than a measurable model.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Use Klaviyo metrics as flow triggers and personalisation filters
cards.summary: Treat metrics (events) as the automation engine: they trigger flows and define who receives what.
cards.use_when: Building or debugging flows, especially abandoned checkout/cart, and building personalised dynamic content.
steps: Understand the three metric sources: Klaviyo-native (received email, opened, clicked, unsubscribed, marked spam, dropped), Shopify (ordered product, placed order, fulfilled, refunded, checkout started, order cancelled), and API/integration events from other apps.
Use metrics as flow triggers. The source's example: the 'Checkout Started' metric triggers the abandoned-checkout flow, with the first email sent about 2 hours later.
Use metrics as filters and conditions for who should receive an email and who should not — e.g. don't send a first-purchase offer to someone with a 'Placed Order' metric in their history.
Use metric properties for personalisation — an order metric carries what was purchased and for how much, enabling conditional and dynamic content.
Confirm each required event is actually firing end-to-end (place a test order, start a test checkout) before relying on it as a trigger, since missing metrics mean silent flow failures.
caveats: Because events drive triggers, a broken integration produces no errors — flows simply never fire. Test after every app or theme change.
Event names differ between Shopify and any custom API implementations; map them deliberately.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Read a Klaviyo profile to decide segmentation and personalisation
cards.summary: Use the profile page as the single richest record of a customer — subscription source, custom properties, predictive analytics, event timeline — to drive filters and dynamic content.
cards.use_when: Designing segments, splits and conditional content, or investigating why one customer received the wrong message.
steps: Check subscription status first: email/SMS opt-in state, how and when they subscribed, and which form they used. This determines whether they are mailable at all.

Review custom properties, which are brand-specific: source, prospect vs repeat purchaser flags, Shopify tags pulled through the integration, loyalty points balance. These are the fields you can filter on.
Review standard data: language, location (from IP or checkout address), most recent acquisition source, last site visit, profile created/updated timestamps, first/last active.
Read the event timeline on the right side to reconstruct the journey — active on site, submitted form, subscribed, each email open, product views, orders.
Open Metrics & Insights and edit which metrics appear at a glance (orders placed, revenue, fulfilled). Add loyalty or other integration metrics if useful.

Use predictive analytics fields: predicted CLV, predicted date of next order, and channel affinity (which channel the person prefers) to avoid double-sending email plus SMS to someone who prefers one channel.
Use recently viewed products for dynamic content — show that person the products they actually looked at rather than a static recommendation block.
caveats: Predictive analytics are model outputs and should inform, not dictate, targeting; the source frames them as attribution/hint data.
Custom properties only exist if you or an integration creates them; a missing property cannot be used as a filter.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Organise profiles into lists and segments, and never campaign to the whole list
cards.summary: Keep static lists for opt-in sources and welcome-flow triggers; use dynamic engagement-filtered segments for campaigns.
cards.use_when: Campaign sending setup, list growth tracking, or troubleshooting welcome flows sending the wrong message.
steps: Maintain one primary email list and one primary SMS list for organic opt-ins (pop-up forms and checkout). This concentrates welcome-flow triggering for your main traffic source.
Use lists for opt-ins and as welcome/nurture flow triggers only — lists are static and never change membership once a person is added.

Create separate lists for each non-organic import or campaign source (e.g. an Instagram giveaway). Reason 1: track how each source contributes to list growth. Reason 2: control welcome messaging — an Instagram giveaway subscriber should get a giveaway welcome, not the '10% off your first order' welcome.
Build dynamic segments for sending campaigns. Segments update continuously based on behaviour, purchase status, engagement and other profile data.
Apply the rule the source states emphatically: never send a campaign to your entire list, and it is rare to send to a list at all. Segments protect deliverability and personalisation.
Confirm each list has a distinct associated welcome flow before importing, so the flow-to-source mapping is not accidental.
caveats: Multiple lists mean multiple welcome flows to maintain; be deliberate about adding new ones.
List membership is permanent for people once added, so list-based sending will accumulate stale contacts — another reason to send via segments.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Build the engaged prospect and engaged customer segments
cards.summary: Create engagement-qualified segments that separate first-time prospects from returning customers, then use the campaign results to learn what converts each group.
cards.use_when: Setting up your campaign sending audience, or improving deliverability and personalisation for campaigns.
steps: Apply the core principle: only send campaigns to people who have shown they want to hear from you. Continuing to send to a subscriber who has not opened or clicked in two years is a certain negative signal with no upside.

Define engagement with OR conditions: opened email in the last 180 days (Apple privacy open = false) OR clicked email in the last 180 days (bot click = false) OR subscribed to a list in the last 14 days OR active on site at least once in the last 14 days.
Add the mailability condition AND can/cannot receive email marketing, so unsubscribed and suppressed profiles are excluded even if they meet other criteria.
Then split the segment into (a) prospects who have never purchased and (b) existing customers, and create both as reusable segments for every campaign send.

Rationale for splitting: after each campaign you can see purchase results by segment, distinguishing first-order conversion from repeat purchases. A single blended engaged segment hides whether a campaign acquired or retained.

Extend the split to brand-relevant axes where useful — the source's example is an apparel brand separating male-buyer and female-buyer history to see whether women's campaigns are being bought by men.
Keep engagement criteria attached to every derived segment, including interest-based ones. A customer who has purchased ten times but never opens email still hurts deliverability if mailed.
caveats: The 180-day and 14-day windows are the source's chosen thresholds, not proven optima; adjust to your purchase cycle.
The prospect/customer split is a reporting and learning device first; targeting value is a secondary benefit.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Style campaign creative by segment learning
cards.summary: Once prospect vs customer is separated, read which creative elements converted each group and repeat those elements in the channel aimed at that group.
cards.use_when: Writing campaign and welcome-series creative, or deciding what proof and offers to lead with for new vs returning buyers.
steps: Send campaigns to the split segments from the previous card so results are attributable to prospect or customer audiences.

After the send, compare conversion between segments and note which content elements appear to drive the result. The source's illustrative example: if a prospect-heavy campaign featuring lots of reviews converts prospects well, add more reviews to prospect-facing campaigns and to the welcome series.

Carry the learning forward by audience, not across the board: what works for first-time buyers does not automatically work for repeat buyers, because the two groups buy for fundamentally different reasons.

Apply the same logic to discounts: prospect segments are where first-purchase offers belong; customer segments should receive non-discount value (new arrivals, replenishment, loyalty, education) instead.
Iterate by changing one creative variable per send so the comparison remains interpretable.
caveats: This is a directional learning loop, not a controlled creative test; the source presents it as observed practice rather than a measured effect size.
Do not generalise a prospect creative win to customers without checking, and vice versa.
cards.source_name: 2026 Klaviyo Email Marketing Full Course (3+ Hours).docx

cards.title: Employ retention and account-level setup: where email sits in the 2026 lifecycle
cards.summary: Commit to a measured email cadence and a five-flow automated core, then extend with gamification, zero-party-data quizzes and split desktop/mobile experiences.
cards.use_when: Roadmapping the lifecycle programme, deciding sending frequency, and prioritising which automations to build first.
steps: Set the base sending cadence at 3–4 campaigns per week, the source's recommended campaign frequency. Consistency matters as much as volume for reputation — erratic bursts are a negative signal.
Prioritise the five core Klaviyo automated flows: Welcome, Browse Abandonment, Abandoned Cart, Abandoned Checkout and Post-Purchase. These are the standard set to build before advanced work.
Give the welcome flow a fast clock: the first 72 hours after signup is the critical conversion window, with day zero driving the highest purchase volume. Put your best converting email first.

After the core is in place, add advanced tactics the source lists: active gamification such as spin-to-win or scratch-off capture, zero-party data collection quizzes, and separate split-tested desktop and mobile experiences rather than one responsive template.

Recognise that the inbox itself is now AI-curated (e.g. Gmail's AI inbox), so authentication, regular cleaning and engagement-tiered segmentation are the levers that put mail in the primary inbox rather than the promotions tab.
Track cadence, flow coverage and inbox placement as programme health metrics, and be prepared to iterate rather than set and forget.
caveats: 3–4 campaigns per week plus flow volume is aggressive for some audiences; the source also tells you to learn whether emails are wanted, so cadence should be validated against engagement and spam complaints.
The 72-hour welcome window and day-zero concentration are the source's observations across an agency portfolio, not a guarantee for every offer type.
